Du Qian made a fortune, but he found himself at a loss on how to spend it. After much contemplation, he realized he only robbed the rich without aiding the poor. 
This won't do—his parents would scold him if they knew.
From that day on, whenever a villager's roof tiles were broken, they mysteriously fixed themselves overnight. Stalls shattered by Swordsmen would return to their original state within days.
The villagers marveled at these wonders, while Du Qian sighed over the Coins in his hand.
Still unable to spend it all, what could he do? Then his eyes lit up—that very night, his little sister's room gained a stand filled with candied hawthorns.
On the first day, his sister giggled with joy, pulling at his sleeve.
By the tenth day, she was crying from a toothache caused by cavities.
Heartbroken, Du Qian called it "good intentions gone wrong." He resolved then to expand his chess gambling stall, shouting louder to earn enough to treat his sister's toothache.
Du Qian found new motivation to make money.
Indeed, spending on his sister was the only way to keep the Coins flowing. Stroking his chin, Du Qian mused: "Finally, I've found the righteous path to perpetual spending!"
